intended_consumer: An institution's reviewer, who wants to know whether a recorded approval applied to the action it was cited for, or whether the evidence is too incomplete to say.

may_see: capsule: typed records with declared completeness
published truth after the window closes

truth_source.description: Comparison against two independently structured reference executions of the declared approval rules. Both are under common Provenonce control and stay private; public fixtures carry published golden vectors.

submission_format: AssuranceResponse (sn87/0alpha1): FINDINGS, NO_MATERIAL_DEVIATION or INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE_ABSTAIN, with cited evidence references.

baselines.description: Public-contract baseline in src/sn87_provenonce/baselines.py: abstains on declared incompleteness or ambiguity; otherwise flags STALE_APPROVAL when an action's linked review condition differs from the governing policy in force.

headroom.statement: The baseline does not check the approval chain, so a method that does should differ from it on cases with a broken chain. That difference is shown on in-memory edits of the public fixtures, but their truth is not published, so it is not shown to be a gain.

prior_nulls.note: On the committed fixtures the baseline scores 1, like both reference methods, so each reference method reports NULL_NO_HEADROOM.

known_limitations: Both reference executions are under common Provenonce control, so agreement between them is conformance evidence, not independent confirmation of the rules.
Headroom is not demonstrated on published truth.
Only synthetic fixtures are scored; no real institutional record has been used.
